prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1245; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured's driver, who is named on the policy. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of impact. The other driver gave a statement that matches the sequence described at first notice.

Entry 3: Photographs of both vehicles were reviewed. The damage pattern is consistent with the reported impact, and the front-end deformation lines up across both cars.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed. No prior damage to the affected areas is known from the claim file or the vehicle history, and nothing suggests any of the damage predates the policy's coverage start.

Entry 5: Claimant reported neck pain and stiffness at the first medical visit. The reported injury is a common result of the kind and force of this type of collision.

Entry 6: Medical records received. Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy and a short run of medication, and the claimant's symptoms eased steadily as they improved.

Entry 7: Attorney's office confirmed the claimant's account. The claimant has given the same description of events in every conversation so far, including the initial call, the recorded statement, and the follow-up interview.

Entry 8: Reviewed prior medical history with the claimant's authorization. No earlier injury to the neck or upper back is documented, and no prior claims involving the same body area appear in the index search.

Entry 9: Treating provider's notes show progressive improvement with reduced visit frequency over the following weeks. The treatment timeline is in line with a typical soft-tissue recovery.

Entry 10: Witness statements, photographs, and the other driver's account all confirm the collision occurred as described. No conflicting information has been found in the file.

Entry 11: Claim reviewed against all available documentation. The injury, treatment course, vehicle damage, and account of events are consistent with one another, and the file is ready for settlement evaluation with counsel.
